title: Grab Redesigns Counter Service Storage for 50% Lower P99 Latency
gist: Grab moved its anti-fraud Counter Service from a wide-column database to Aerospike with a redesigned data model, reporting about 50% lower p99 read latency, data cut from 3 TB to 1 TB, and 45-50% lower per-node cost, with no downtime.

insights.claim: Grab reports about 50% lower production p99 read latency after moving Counter Service to Aerospike.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Datastore choice can halve tail latency on high-throughput fraud paths.
insights.locator: Grab reports roughly 50% lower production p99 read latency

insights.claim: On-disk data fell from about 3 TB to 1 TB and cost per node dropped 45% to 50%.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Material infrastructure savings for Aerospike over wide-column in this workload.
insights.locator: a reduction in on-disk data from about 3 TB to 1 TB

insights.claim: The service supports Grab's anti-fraud platform at tens of thousands of queries per second, about one billion requests per day.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Illustrates scale of fraud-detection counters at a Southeast Asian super-app.
insights.locator: handling tens of thousands of queries per second

insights.claim: Aerospike keeps roughly 64 bytes of primary-index metadata per record, so a row-per-time-bucket model made record count a capacity problem.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Cardinality, not data size, drives Aerospike memory cost; model data accordingly.

insights.claim: Grab consolidated all time buckets of a counter into one record holding a timestamp-ordered map, cutting record count by more than an order of magnitude.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Consolidating records is the key lever for Aerospike efficiency.

insights.claim: Moving from server-side time-range filtering to client-side filtering of map records, plus Aerospike's batch API, reduced network round trips for multi-key reads.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Trading server-side filtering for batching can reduce latency in multi-key workloads.

insights.claim: Grab put a storage facade with legacy, Aerospike and mock implementations in front of its Rust service and ramped shadow reads from 5% to 20%, 50%, 100% before shifting live traffic.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A reusable zero-downtime datastore migration pattern.

insights.claim: During rollout Grab hit issues in the Aerospike Rust client, including an initially synchronous API and DNS handling in cluster replacement, and worked with upstream maintainers.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Aerospike's Rust client maturity is a risk for Rust-based adopters.
insights.locator: During rollout, Grab also encountered issues
